title: What Buyers in the Gulf Actually Look For
excerpt: A breakdown of quality, packaging and documentation expectations across UAE agricultural importers.
content:
## Why documentation matters first

Most rejected shipments to the UAE aren't rejected for quality — they're rejected for paperwork. Before quality is even inspected, importers check for a valid **phytosanitary certificate**, correct **HS code classification**, and a certificate of origin that matches the invoice exactly.

## Packaging expectations

Gulf buyers generally expect produce packed for a hot-climate supply chain: ventilated cartons, consistent unit weights, and clear country-of-origin labeling in both English and Arabic where required.

## What this means for a small exporter

Start every shipment by confirming paperwork with your buyer's clearing agent *before* the goods leave the port — not after.

title: Reading Your Soil Before You Plant
excerpt: A simple, no-equipment method for judging soil health before committing a season to it.
content:
## The squeeze test

Take a handful of moist soil and squeeze it. If it holds a loose shape and crumbles when poked, you likely have a healthy loam. If it turns to a hard ball, your soil is clay-heavy and will need organic matter worked in before planting.

## What to look for beyond texture

Healthy soil smells earthy, not sour. Sour or metallic smells often indicate poor drainage or compaction, both of which stress root systems.

## A five-minute habit worth keeping

Before every planting season, take this test in three different spots on your land — soil quality is rarely uniform across a full plot.
